episodes.title: What it means when AI helps solve complex math problems
episodes.about: In September, OpenAI said that its models had solved one of math's famous Millennium Prize problems. Then, the lab dropped more than 700 papers tackling another 400 complex problems with more breakthroughs to come. These developments have caused something of an existential crisis in the math world. But Alex Kontorovich, a professor of math at Rutgers University, says they're a gift.
episodes.why: Out today: Rutgers mathematician Alex Kontorovich on why OpenAI's run of solved problems - a Millennium Prize problem, then 700-plus papers on 400 more - is a gift to math, not just a crisis for it.

episodes.title: AI Won’t Make Our Minds Useless According to 400 Years of History
episodes.about: What if abundant intelligence makes human ambition expand rather than human relevance disappear? NLW explores Venkatesh Rao's “Cognitive Mercantilism,” which uses the history of capitalism to challenge assumptions about AI and our intellectual future. From the agricultural revolution to today's AI agents, the episode examines how cheaper intelligence could unlock new desires, new work, and possibilities we haven't yet imagined.
episodes.why: Venkatesh Rao's 'Cognitive Mercantilism' argues cheaper intelligence expands what people want and attempt, traced from the agricultural revolution to today's agents.

episodes.title: The Disappearing Amateur Conundrum
episodes.about: For generations, becoming good at something meant spending a considerable amount of time being bad at it. A teenager learning guitar struggled through chords before playing a complete song. An aspiring photographer took hundreds of disappointing pictures before developing an eye for composition. Someone interested in writing spent years learning how to turn scattered thoughts into compelling stories. Most people never became professionals, and that was never the point. AI is changing this relationship between interest, effort, and accomplishment: someone with little musical training now has access to tools that produce sophisticated compositions, an aspiring filmmaker creates scenes without mastering cameras, lighting, or editing software, and a person with no programming experience builds a functional application by describing what they want.
episodes.why: AI tools now let beginners skip the years of being bad at guitar, photography, or writing - and this asks what is lost when the amateur stage disappears.

episodes.title: AI chatbots can make election fakes. Can they spot them?
episodes.about: You used to need a government-backed operation to spread election disinformation. Now a chatbot might do. Larry Norden of the Brennan Center put the major AI chatbots to the test: Could they create election fakes? Debunk them? Even recognize their own handiwork? The answers were not all reassuring.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Click Here is Recorded Future News' cybersecurity show, new here: the Brennan Center tested whether the big chatbots can create election fakes, debunk them, and recognize their own work - tested just before Election Day.

episodes.title: Was I wrong about open models & cyber risks?
episodes.about: Last week coined the term “Black October” after an onslaught of critical vulnerability disclosures, including PHP2Shell and a long-standing GitLab bug, signified the moment when the cyber risks of AI models started to materialize. Nathan Lambert asks whether the Binance security incident changes that picture, and argues we are living through an exponential rise in vulnerabilities that will take a long time to level off, even as the behind-the-scenes work of patching the internet accelerates.
episodes.why: Discovery pick — Interconnects is Nathan Lambert's AI research analysis show, new here: after Black October's vulnerability flood, he re-examines whether he was wrong about the cyber risks of open models, in 10 minutes.
